Reportedly, Apple has been working with LG to develop "second-party" Home accessories, but new information suggests that "second-party" smart home products may also come from another company.

iOS 27.2 code reveals a new Home accessory set to appear as a "second-party" product, not from LG

Over the past day, we have seen multiple reports about Apple's ambitions to expand its smart home ecosystem.

In addition to its own Home products expected to launch next week — such as the new Apple TV 4K, "HomePad", and HomePod mini 2 — the company has reportedly been collaborating with LG on a range of new home accessories.

These accessories are co-manufactured by Apple and LG but will be sold under the LG brand. Leaked images revealed today give us a glimpse of what they look like:

  • Leaked images reveal new Home smart door locks, thermostats, and other products designed by Apple for LG
  • Apple's new Home camera and doorbell co-developed with LG exposed in leaked images

Apple's idea of strengthening its smart home ecosystem through co-developed products makes a lot of sense. In fact, this partnership may not be limited to LG alone.

Leaker pdfu discovered two additional Home accessories in the iOS 27.2 code, marked as "second-party" products.

These accessories are Schneider-branded smart thermostats and temperature/humidity sensors.

According to pdfu's post, currently only the new LG accessories and these two Schneider products are labelled as "second-party" in Apple's HomeKit database.

Accessories classified as second-party will "receive special treatment from the operating system."

It remains unclear whether Apple is working as closely with Schneider on accessory development as it reportedly is with LG. However, the code appears to suggest so.

What do you think of Apple's reportedly new Home product strategy? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
